title: Amplifying Perceived Value Techniques
opening: When effort fills your attention, a supported value or result can become hard to see. Reconnect it with evidence. A compelling explanation cannot make an ineffective activity valuable.

labels.exampleIntro: Illustrative case. An instructor is tired of correcting the same worked example and wants learners to use the method independently.
labels.workedValue: Learners can use the method independently.
labels.workedEffects: In this fictional two-learner check, one learner used the revised explanation to solve a new problem without a prompt. A second still needed a hint at the first step.
labels.workedWider: The example has not been checked in a class or reused by other instructors. A wider effect is not established.
labels.workedProgress: The instructor revised one confusing label and tried the example with two learners. One result supports independent use; the other shows a remaining gap.
labels.workedUnresolved: Why did the second learner need a hint? Does the revision help beyond these two tries? How much time does repeated correction take?
labels.continueMessage: The independent solution is one concrete effect worth checking again. Continue only with a bounded next test: inspect where the hint was needed, try the revised explanation, and record both results. That plan is not evidence of a broader contribution.
labels.changeMessage: The remaining hint and unknown wider results matter too. Change the arrangement to address the point of confusion; if actual use contradicts the claimed benefit, revise the pursuit. Stopping can fit when the value is no longer there.
labels.reconsiderMessage: If actual use keeps contradicting the claimed benefit, reconsider or stop the pursuit. Do not turn a possible future contribution into evidence that it already helps.
labels.practiceIntro: Name the value, inspect observed effects and real progress, keep contrary evidence visible, and choose a response that the evidence supports. Write one useful summary to save; the other responses may stay blank. A projected benefit is not an achieved result.
labels.choicePrompt: Choose a response to the example

practice.prediction: What core value does this pursuit serve? (Optional)
practice.observation: What concrete effect has actually occurred, and who observed it? Separate the result from what you hope will happen. (Optional)
practice.comparison: What wider contribution is supported, and what remains unshown? (Optional)
practice.result: What progress is recorded? What contrary evidence or unresolved facts remain? (Optional)
practice.revision: Would you continue with a bounded check or change the arrangement or pursuit? What evidence could change your answer? (Optional)
practice.step: One useful summary or next action to keep from this comparison (required to save)
